events.summary: 8 edges from login_access_token, 4 inside the repo.

steps.explanation: This route is the entry point for OAuth2 password-flow login.

claims.text: POST /api/v1/login/access-token is defined in backend/app/api/routes/login.py at line 23.
POST /api/v1/login/access-token is handled by login_access_token.

steps.explanation: The login handler takes the submitted form and authenticates the user by email and password.

claims.text: POST /api/v1/login/access-token routes to login_access_token at line 23.
The handler receives OAuth2 form data with username and password.
It passes the form username as email plus password to crud.authenticate.

steps.explanation: Authenticate loads the user row and checks the password hash; deeper lookup and hash helpers were read but not followed as separate graph steps.

claims.text: login_access_token calls authenticate at line 30.
Authenticate looks up the user by email.
It verifies the plain password against the stored hashed_password and returns the user only if verified.

steps.explanation: After authentication returns, the handler enforces active status and issues a timed token.

claims.text: login_access_token calls authenticate at line 30.
If authenticate returns no user, login raises Incorrect email or password.
claims.quote: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Incorrect email or password")

claims.text: If the user is inactive, login rejects with Inactive user.
On success it builds an expiry time from settings and calls security.create_access_token with user.id.

steps.explanation: This creates the signed JWT access token returned to the client for future requests.

claims.text: login_access_token calls create_access_token at line 39.
The token payload contains expiry exp and subject sub from the user id.
It JWT-encodes the payload with SECRET_KEY and returns the token string.
